title: A study of the vascular complications associated with the transfemoral approach in transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI)
summary:
In order to provide patients with the best possible advice on which of the available procedures should be used for the optimal treatment of heart valve disease, key findings from preliminary investigations are assessed. These include, for example, age, laboratory test results, clinical history, current medication, and X-ray, ultrasound echocardiography and CT scans, in order to assess the condition, size and pumping function of the heart, the affected heart valves and the blood vessels.
The planned minimally invasive heart valve implantation will be carried out via a blood vessel in the groin. This requires a blood vessel of sufficient size; in other words, the internal diameter must be large enough for the system to pass through. After implantation, the blood vessel must be closed off again. A possible complication during the operation could be subsequent bleeding from the vessel. To prevent this, various standard occlusion systems are used. The aim of the study is to determine which system works best – that is, one that both prevents bleeding and is gentle enough to ensure that no narrowing of the blood vessel remains at the closure site. 
The standard procedure for the preparation, performance and aftercare of the heart valve implantation remains unchanged. 
The choice of which closure system is used after implantation will be determined by random allocation (randomisation).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Severe aortic valve stenosis
• Positive recommendation from the cardiac team for TAVI via the transfemoral approach
• Standard TAVI planning CT scan
Exclusion criteria:
• Age < 18 years
• Acute coronary syndrome
• Urgent or emergency TAVI implantation
• History of primary haemorrhagic diathesis
• Secondary increased risk of bleeding (e.g. liver cirrhosis)
• Requirement for dialysis
• Lack of consent/capacity to consent
• Pregnancy
